messages:
incident-bot: pager triggered: 4xx increase on billing/emit pipeline; token-emit-rate dropped ~70% for a subset of customers (12). Auto-escalation to #incidents. https://redwood.ops/alerts/1789012345 :rotating_light:
maya: seeing the alert, pulling dashboard now. which emitter?
sam: looks like emitter-prod-3 in eu-west-1 is quiet. metric: token_emitted_per_min by emitter shows flatline at 0.
jules: @maya @sam ok can you run last-1h query on raw ingest counts vs billing emits? want to know gap size.
maya: running query -> lines:
```sql
SELECT region, emitter_id, SUM(tokens_ingested) AS ingested, SUM(tokens_emitted) AS emitted
FROM metering.emits
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY region, emitter_id;
```
maya: results: eu-west-1 emitter-prod-3 ingested=1,240,000 emitted=380,000 (approx 860k delta) — multiple customer streams affected including ACME_CORP and brightleaf-app.
eli: that delta will definitely trigger overage flags for some customers if not reconciled. we should mark impacted accounts and pause alerts to billing until we know full backfill plan.
sam: quick triage: emitter process shows OOMs in logs then restarted repeatedly over last 45m. tail excerpt:
```
2026-02-14T09:12:22Z emitter[pid=2489]: ERROR OOM while allocating kv cache
2026-02-14T09:12:22Z emitter[pid=2489]: restarting service
2026-02-14T09:13:10Z emitter[pid=2610]: started
2026-02-14T09:18:05Z emitter[pid=2610]: steady state
```

jules: OOM cycle could explain emit suppression. are we on v2 emitter with new memory limits?
maya: yes, emitter image v2.4 rolled two days ago. resource requests were lowered in the last patch. paging metering infra.
eli: mitigation plan suggestions: 1) scale emitter-prod-3 to 0 and back to force clean start; 2) roll back to v2.3 or increase memory; 3) enable shadow-emitter-v1 in same AZ to drain backlog; 4) notify billing to avoid charging on incomplete emits.
sam: I'm going to scale up a hot standby and kick off backfill job. running:
```
kubectl -n metering scale deployment/emitter-prod-3 --replicas=3 && kubectl rollout restart deployment/emitter-prod-3 -n metering
```

sam: also starting backfill for last 2 hours: `python tools/backfill.py --from now-2h --to now --scope emitter-prod-3`
jules: @metering-bot can you stash current emit sequence numbers for replay? we need deterministic backfill.
metering-bot: stashed sequences: emitter-prod-3 seq_start=5823412 seq_end=5829801. backfill ticket created: MET-8471.
maya: notifying ops and billing: tagging impacted customers for manual crediting if needed. drafting message to accounts team now.
eli: temporary alert actions: suppress overage alert rules for the impacted customer IDs until backfill completes. created alert ticket: A-6783.
sam: hot-standby v1 is up and consuming backlog, I'm seeing emit rate climb back to ~85% within 10m. logs show fewer OOMs after increasing memory limit.
jules: excellent. keep oncall handoff to metering team once stable. next steps: 1) finish backfill, 2) reconcile token tallies, 3) run cost/regression check, 4) postmortem about v2 resource tuning.
maya: assigning to metering oncall @jules for follow-up. leave the thread open until backfill complete.
eli: customer comms draft: "We detected reduced usage visibility for some customers between 09:10-09:55 UTC due to an emitter process restart. We are backfilling missing usage and will reconcile billing; no customer charges will be applied for the missing tokens. ETA for reconciliation 4 hours." please review.
jules: LGTM. i’ll own reconciliation and postmortem. adding runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/metering-emit :eyes:
metering-bot: backfill progress: 30% complete (estimated finish +2h).
maya: marking incident as mitigation_in_progress. will update status page with minimal incident note to avoid duplicate customer alarms. :white_check_mark:
